newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLAND OPTIMISTIC ABOUT 2006 WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND OPTIMISTIC ABOUT 2006 WORLD CUP.

text.p: Graham Kelly, the chief executive of the English Football Association said on Friday he was "very confident" England's bid for the 2006 World Cup bid would prove successful.

Kelly agreed the FA faced tough competition for the tournament, particularly from Germany, but in an interview on BBC television said he was optimistic about England staging the World Cup in 10 years time.
"We have a very good chance indeed. By any standards 1996 was a wonderful and exciting year. On the back of Euro 96 we announced the World Cup bid.

"We are very confident. We are talking to people all the time, making friends. We have the backing of the government, the Sports Council, the major clubs and of course this week the announcement about the new national stadium at Wembley.
"It will be a state-of-the-art modern stadium for the next century. We don't know the exact design yet -- we will be sitting down to discuss that."
The new Wembley is also intended to cater for athletics and rugby league, but soccer and the World Cup are at the top of the agenda.
"We are very confident we have a very strong bid _-- we have shown our capabilities in 1996, now we are looking to pursue the bid with a great deal of confidence," said Kelly.
"The Germans are very powerful on and off the pitch, so we look forward to maintaining our keen rivalry with them."
England staged the World Cup in 1966, while Germany hosted the tournament eight years later. Both countries won the World Cup as host nation.
